abstract_summary: Long-horizon dialogue agents need to keep user memories stable enough for personalization while adapting when the user genuinely changes. Given the recall outputs (Ct,s t) and the new interaction (ut, yt), PreCoMem computes a prediction-
error signal adjusted by retrieval reliability, and applies a regime-gated update to the belief store. It
also writes the new turn back into the episodic cache for future provenance and recall.
Retrieval reliability.Surprisal computed against recalled evidence can be misleading when recall is
uncertain, so we derive a reliability coefficient from the entropy of retrieval scores. Let st ={s i}|Ct|i=1
denote the Top-K retrieval scores returned withCt, and let ˆsi = (si +ϵ)/ Pj(sj +ϵ) be the smoothed
normalization. We define the normalized entropyH t and the reliability coefficientρ t as
Ht = − Pi ˆsi log ˆsilog max{|Ct|,2} ∈[0,1], ρ t = 1−H t.(3)
Because Ht is minimized when one item dominates and maximized under near-uniform scores, ρt
measures score concentration as a proxy for evidence

Evaluation protocol.We adopt the LLM-as-a-judge protocol from MemOS [ 18]: each answer is
scored by a primary judge (gpt-4.1-mini) and two auxiliarygemini-2.5-flashjudges (run with distinct
system prompts to reduce judge-correlation) in a blinded setup, with accuracy reported as the average
of the three binary judgments [39–43]. Appendix Section C.3 reports human–LLM agreement on
LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S, and DiMoBench plus a cross-method spot-check on baseline outputs.
Implementation details.PreCoMem usesgpt-4.1(orgpt-4o-mini) for all LLM-based reasoning
and memory operations andQwen3-Embedding-0.6B for dense embeddings across methods. Un-
less otherwise specified, k=10, (θlow, θhigh) = (0.2,0.6) , λ=0.5, β=1.0, α=(0.4,0.4,0.2) , and
γ=0.05; sensitivity studies and the adaptive variant are in Appendix Section C.5.

A natural concern for any long-term memory system is whether storage and retrieval cost scale
gracefully with the conversation length. We examine this on three settings spanning natural and
stress-test horizons: the LoCoMo benchmark (ten multi-session dialogues, mean ¯N= 588 turns),
DiMoBench (350 turns, 1 drift), and DiMoBench-XL (1050 turns, 3 drifts; five personas, of which
a representative one is plotted, the others staying within ±1.4 of it; Appendix Section C.6). Two
quantities are tracked every 10 turns on DiMoBench and every 50 turns on DiMoBench-XL:

across LoCoMo (199-QA stratified audit), LongMemEval -S (full 500
QAs), and DiMoBench (200-QA audit covering one canonical persona), thegpt-4.1-miniprimary
judge agrees with expert human re-annotation at 96.9% overall (93.8–98.5% per question type) with
Cohen's κ between 0.81 and 0.96 in every question type (0.957, 0.878 and 0.821 at the dataset level
for LoCoMo, LongMemEval -S and DiMoBench). κ is lowest on DiMoBench, which combines
the lowest agreement (95.4%) with a high chance-agreement baseline: both raters mark about 85%
of its answers correct, so more of the agreement is expected by chance than on LoCoMo, where
about 72% are marked correct. To rule out the concern that the judge might be calibrated only
on PreCoMem outputs, we additionally re-ran the same human-vs-judge study on 50 outputs each
from the two strongest baselines (EverMemOS and TiMem) on LoCoMo and LongMemEval

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Per-category human-LLM agreement audits with Cohen's kappa from 0.81 to 0.96 and objective benchmark ground-truth state probes corroborate the automated evaluation verdicts.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Tri-judge LLM evaluation (primary gpt-4.1-mini and two gemini-2.5-flash auxiliary judges) measuring end-task question answering accuracy across benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Turn-level effective surprisal computed from NLI contradiction scoring and cosine semantic deviation, gated deterministically into update rules parameterized by bounded LLM sub-agent scalars.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding improved handling of belief drift, reduced old-memory pull, and memory scalability with bounded effective memory mass are directly corroborated by empirical results, trajectory analyses, and sensitivity sweeps.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is evaluated extensively across multiple established benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S, PersonaMem-v2, AMemGym, LoCoMo-Plus) and a newly introduced drift benchmark (DiMoBench), demonstrating consistent performance gains over modern baselines. Detailed ablation studies isolate the contributions of effective surprisal, confidence weighting, and individual update operators.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Per-category human-LLM agreement audits (with Cohen's kappa from 0.81 to 0.96) and objective benchmark ground-truth state probes corroborate the automated evaluation verdicts.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Tri-judge LLM evaluation (primary gpt-4.1-mini and two gemini-2.5-flash auxiliary judges) measuring end-task question answering accuracy across benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Turn-level effective surprisal computed via NLI contradiction scoring and cosine semantic deviation, gated deterministically into update rules parameterized by bounded LLM sub-agent scalars.

primary.limitations: The work explicitly documents limitations including turn-level vs. per-item update routing granularity, the reliance on initial Top-k retrieval to detect update-due events, and its current restriction to English dialogue settings.
primary.method_assessment: PreCoMem provides a clear hybrid execution model combining deterministic closed-form confidence updates and retrieval-entropy reliability weighting with bounded scalar proposals from specialized LLM sub-agents. The memory structure cleanly separates mutable beliefs from an immutable episodic trace cache.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a conceptually grounded, mathematically specified, and thoroughly evaluated framework. The empirical validation is exemplary, combining multi-benchmark testing, human audit validation of automated judges, factorial ablations, and thorough latency/scalability profiling.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces PreCoMem, a long-term memory framework for conversational dialogue agents that models memories as confidence-weighted beliefs updated via a predictive coding-inspired effective surprisal gate routing into maintain, profile (hypothesis buffering), or correct operations.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a conceptually grounded, mathematically specified, and thoroughly evaluated framework. The empirical validation is exemplary, combining multi-benchmark testing, human audit validation of automated judges, factorial ablations, and thorough latency/scalability profiling.
